Tell the machine what to do. It happens, often in parallel.

gozer is cooperative chip leasing for Tenstorrent boxes. Several agents, apps and scripts can share one machine, and each one gets the chips it asked for when its turn comes.

Your agents and apps do not need their own routine for asking politely for hardware. They queue up, keep working on other things until chips are free, do their work on the hardware, and carry on. Everyone gets a turn.

Install on Debian or Ubuntu

$$ sudo apt install ./tt-gozer_${version}_all.deb

Download the .deb file from the latest release, then run the line above in the folder you saved it to.

How it works

  1. A lease for each board. You ask for a number of chips. gozer leases a whole board, because the Tenstorrent runtime's device visibility works at board level: a grant of one chip can expose both chips on its board. Each agent points the runtime at the chips it was given, so two agents on two boards stay out of each other's way.
  2. A queue. If no board is free, you get a ticket and a place in line. Your agent can keep doing work that needs no chips. When it runs gozer wait with the ticket, gozer hands it the chips as soon as a board is released.
  3. A check that a chip is really in use. A lease record only says who asked. gozer also looks for an open device file under /dev/tenstorrent, which proves a process is using the chip. When a lease's process has ended and its device is closed, gozer clears the lease the next time someone asks for chips. A lease taken by a bare gozer acquire has no process to watch, so gozer clears it only after 900 seconds (15 minutes) have passed since the grant with no device open. Either way, a crashed agent cannot hold a board forever.
$diagram

What gozer does not do

gozer is cooperative. Any local user can release any lease, so it works because everyone on the box uses it. It does not stop a program that opens the chips without asking.

Install

gozer is a small Python program. It needs Python 3.10 or newer, and tt-smi to reset chips. The Debian package is a single architecture-independent file for Debian and Ubuntu.

  1. Install the package from the latest release. 
    $$ sudo apt install ./tt-gozer_${version}_all.deb
  2. Link the three Claude Code skills into your own ~/.claude/skills, so Claude Code knows to lease chips before it uses them. 
    $$ gozer-install-skills
  3. See the state of the box. 
    $$ gozer status

From a clone of the repository, run ./install.sh to get the same command and skills.
